column1: And if you look at antibiotics, it gets worse.
Niti Aayog — that's the government's own think tank — says out of every hundred rupees India spent on imported antibiotic powder... about eighty-six went to China.
Even your fever tablet has a China link.
Indian factories do make paracetamol powder.
But the raw chemical it's made from?
Industry reports say a big share of that still comes from China.
So you might be thinking — has it always been like this?
Did India ever make its own powder?
It did.
And this part of the story, most people have never heard.
Pimpri, near Pune.
Nineteen fifty-four.
India has been free for less than seven years, and it's building a factory to make its own penicillin.
Penicillin was the miracle drug of that time.
Back then, a small cut on your hand could kill you.
With penicillin, it became a few days of medicine for you.
The government sets up a company called Hindustan Antibiotics.
By nineteen fifty-six, Indian penicillin is coming out of Indian tanks.
Just think about it.
Picture your grandparents' India.
A young, poor country, growing one of the most important medicines on earth... in its own factory.
Soon, others join in — big names you may know, like Alembic, Sarabhai and Ranbaxy.
India is making its own antibiotics.
But to see what happened next, you need to know one thing.
How do you actually make penicillin?
